execution). **Result: -5.354pts — LOSS**, more than THREE TIMES the -1.556pt tightened risk — the
largest close-based-slippage gap yet observed (TRADER_LESSON_019/020), because the tighten decision
had pulled the stop very close to price right before a genuinely large single-bar range (6.2pts,

improvement over not tightening at all: -5.354 vs. what the original 1689.5 stop would likely also
have been jumped through similarly) — but this instance is a clear, disclosable illustration that
tightening a stop very close to current price increases the RELATIVE size of a slippage event even
while reducing the nominal risk figure. Both things are true at once; neither cancels the other.

close the trade here, per the clean-trigger/full-hold/full-exit precedent (trades #11/12/17/23/26/
29/34/36) — not to invent a new reason to hold beyond the plan's own defined target after the fact.

### STOP HIT — TRADE #38 FULL RESOLUTION

Bar 1587704400 (2020-04-24 05:00:00 UTC): O1724.048 H1724.048 L1721.256 **C1722.26** V580 — a clean
close below the tightened stop (1722.5), the first genuine closing violation after 6 prior wicks
below it across 14 bars of compression. Structural invalidation (1720.773) was NOT breached even
intrabar (low 1721.256) — this is a literal-stop exit, not a structural-invalidation exit.

**ENTRY**: 1731.293 (bar 1587648600, 2020-04-23 13:30:00 UTC).
**EXIT**: 1722.26 (bar 1587704400, 2020-04-24 05:00:00 UTC, close-based).
**RESULT**: -9.033pts — **LOSS**.
**DURATION**: 15.5 hours, ~46 M15 bars, including one recurring daily-rollover gap (GAP-038).
**MANAGEMENT USED**: one reactive tighten (1719.5 → 1722.5) after a heavy-volume-stall + breakdown
read (PL-0309), which survived a 3-bar 12,000+ volume contest but ultimately succumbed to a quiet,
thin-volume grind 14 bars later.
**PROCESS_QUALITY**: plan followed exactly — six fields respected throughout, the tighten was
disclosed and reasoned, close-based discipline honored on every one of the 6 prior wicks, and the
exit was taken exactly where the (already-adjusted) frozen stop said it should be. No goalpost-moving
in either direction.

**TRADER_LESSON_023 — realized tighten/stop-out trade-off (first instance where it materialized)**:
had the ORIGINAL stop (1719.5) been left in place instead of tightened, this trade would NOT have
been stopped out here — the lowest wick of the entire post-entry period was 1721.124/1721.782/
1721.256, all comfortably above 1719.5. The tighten (a disclosed, reasoned risk-reduction) is the
proximate and sufficient cause of this loss; the wider original stop was never actually threatened.
This does NOT prove the wider stop was "better" — price might have continued lower and hit 1719.5
too, or the trade might have needed that room specifically because of the volatility the tighten was
reacting to. What it DOES confirm, now with a first realized (not just theoretical) instance: a
proactive tighten trades a smaller loss-if-wrong for a strictly higher probability of being stopped
out by ordinary noise the original stop would have absorbed. TRADER_LESSON_022 named this trade-off
in the abstract (trade #33); this is the first time in the apprenticeship it has been observed to
concretely cost a trade that the original stop, in hindsight, would have survived (at least up to
this point in the log). WHERE_IT_APPLIES: every future tighten decision — the choice should be made
knowing this cost is real and has now happened at least once, not merely theoretical.

**OBSERVATION (extended-compression pattern, not yet a formal candidate)**: this trade also
demonstrates a distinct rhythm from trade #37 — rather than a clean break-and-hold, price spent 14+
bars in tight, thin-volume compression directly on top of a defended-by-the-trader stop before
resolving. Worth watching whether "an extended, thin-volume compression directly on a stop level
(as opposed to a volume-driven contest)" has a different base rate of resolving for vs. against the
position than a heavy-volume contest does — n=1 so far, not enough to say anything.

   `horizontal_line` test DID appear in this same list, confirming the inspection method is sound.

### TRADER_MISTAKE #4 / TRADE #42 CLOSED (immediate write, never buffered) — 1588597200: O1701.384
H1704.404 L1697.678 C1704.198, vol673. Re-examining the bar #17 management decision: at the moment
I "tightened the stop to breakeven, 1700.008," current price (bar #17's own close) was ALREADY at
1701.384 — past that level, against the short. A stop can only protect against FUTURE adverse
movement from the price prevailing when it is set; placing a resting stop at a level the market has
already traded through does not provide real protection, it should instead have been recognized as
"this position needs an immediate at-market exit, not a new resting stop at a stale level." This is a
genuine process mistake, not a market outcome — caught on the very next bar rather than propagated
further, but it should have been caught at the moment the decision was made (bar #17's close), not one
bar later.

Honest ruling: TRADE #42 is closed at the price prevailing when the flawed stop decision was made —
bar #17's close, **1701.384** — not at the nominal "breakeven" figure of 1700.008. Entry 1700.008
(SHORT) / Exit 1701.384 = **-1.376 pts LOSS**. (Independently of this mistake: bar #18's high,
1704.404, would have stopped the original 1703.0 stop out anyway — this trade was not going to survive
this bar regardless. The mistake affects the exit price/attribution, not whether the trade would have
closed.)

LESSON (TRADER_MISTAKE, new): when tightening a stop in reaction to an already-closed bar, check
whether the new stop level has ALREADY been passed by that bar's own close — if so, the position must
be treated as needing an immediate at-market exit at that close price, not a resting stop at a level
current price has already moved beyond.

WORTH_NOTING (not a TOC-003 instance — this floor was only defended twice, not the 3+ TOC-003
requires): a genuine no-stall, real-volume continuation bar (bar #16, vol3352) confirmed the 1702.7
floor break exactly per the continuation-vs-stall discipline, yet the move still fully reversed within
2 bars, reclaiming back above the original reaction high's structure. Continuation-confirmation
raised the odds but did not guarantee the outcome — logged as an adjacent data point, not forced into
TOC-003's own counterexample slot since the precondition (3+ real-volume defenses) genuinely wasn't
met here.

### CEO AUDIT — EXECUTION CONVENTION CORRECTION (2020-05-06, in-replay; triggered by explicit CEO
check on Trade #44)

FINDING: this apprenticeship's authoritative stop-trigger/fill convention, established since Q1 and
reaffirmed repeatedly (TRADER_LESSON_002, TRADER_LESSON_006, TRADER_LESSON_019/020/022 in
AI_TRADER_EXPERIENCE_LEDGER.md), is CLOSE-BASED, NOT intrabar-touch: a stop is only considered
triggered when a bar CLOSES beyond it (a mere wick through the level does not trigger it), and — this
is the part this session got wrong — the FILL PRICE on trigger is that bar's own CLOSE, not the stop
level itself ("the stop is confirmed and priced at that bar's close, not at the level itself").
Trades #42-44 (this session's post-pilot V2 trades) instead used INTRABAR-TOUCH triggering with
fill AT THE STOP PRICE. Trade #42's booked exit happened to already be close-based by coincidence
(the TRADER_MISTAKE_004 fix used the reacting bar's own close, 1701.384, which is what close-based
fill would also produce) — no correction needed there. Trades #43 and #44 did NOT: both used the
literal stop price as the fill, which is wrong under the established convention.

CORRECTION — TRADE #43: triggering bar (T=1588665600) O1698.708 H1709.794 L1697.848 C1703, vol1570.
Under close-based rule, the tightened stop (1699.6) triggers on this bar's CLOSE (1703 > 1699.6) --
same triggering bar as originally identified, but the correct fill price is that bar's CLOSE, 1703,
not the stop level 1699.6. CORRECTED RESULT: entry 1696.401, exit 1703 = **-6.599 pts LOSS** (was
booked as -3.199 pts LOSS -- a genuine loss, correctly categorized as a clean loss-with-a-plan both
before and after this correction, but the magnitude was wrong by 3.4pts).

CORRECTION — TRADE #44: triggering bar (T=1588771800) O1691.859 H1698.036 L1691.826 C1697.896,
vol966. Under close-based rule, the trailed stop (1692.5) triggers on this bar's CLOSE (1697.896 >
1692.5) -- same triggering bar as originally identified, but the correct fill price is that bar's
CLOSE, 1697.896, not the stop level 1692.5. CORRECTED RESULT: entry 1697.443, exit 1697.896 =
**-0.453 pts LOSS** (was booked as +4.943 pts WIN -- this FLIPS the trade from a win to a loss, and
moves it from the "wins with a plan" category to "losses with a plan (clean)"; the six-field plan and
all management decisions were still executed correctly per the frozen contract -- only the fill-price
convention used to score the outcome was wrong).

ROOT CAUSE: this session (post-pilot V2) implicitly reintroduced intrabar-touch stop semantics without
re-deriving them from the established apprenticeship convention -- an unexamined assumption that crept
in silently rather than being a deliberate, reasoned change. Caught only because the CEO explicitly
audited it; not self-caught, which is itself worth naming honestly.

REMEDIATION ADOPTED GOING FORWARD: every future stop/trail check in this apprenticeship uses
CLOSE-BASED triggering (a stop fires only when a bar's CLOSE crosses it, never on a wick alone) and
CLOSE-BASED fill (exit price = that triggering bar's close, never the nominal stop level). This
restores, not invents, the pre-existing convention. STRUCTURAL_INVALIDATION was already being handled
correctly this way throughout (it was always evaluated by close); the defect was specific to literal
INITIAL_STOP/trailing-stop fills.

CORRECTED RUNNING TALLY: 44 trades -- 14 wins with a plan, 1 loss without a plan (mistake), 1 loss via
management-execution mistake (TRADER_MISTAKE_004), 28 losses with a plan (clean, incl. corrected
trades #43 and #44). Net: +15.631 (through trade42, unchanged) + trade43 -6.599 + trade44 -0.453 =
**+8.579 pts net across 44 trades** (previously reported as +17.375 -- the overstatement is fully
attributable to this fill-convention defect, now corrected).

### TRADE #48 -- CLOSED (stop-out, close-based fill; trade-critical immediate write)
TIME: 2020-05-14 17:30:00 UTC (T=1589477400)
BAR: O 1732.278 / H 1732.379 / L 1729.798 / C 1730.03, volume 1407

Bar CLOSE (1730.03) crossed below the live stop level (close-below-1730.264). Per the permanent close-based stop-trigger/fill convention, EXIT PRICE = this bar's own close = 1730.03 (not the nominal stop level 1730.264).

RESULT: entry 1731.446, exit 1730.03 -> **-1.416pts, LOSS-WITH-PLAN (clean)**.

Honest close-out narrative: this trade reached as much as ~+4.034pts unrealized favorable (16:15 UTC, high 1736.158) before giving it all back and closing negative. The stop management itself was disciplined throughout -- entered on 2 consecutive real-volume closes above the 1721.822-1723.654 zone (vol 3492, 8448), trailed twice on genuine rising-lows structure (to 1728.00 then 1730.264), each trail TRADER_MISTAKE_004-checked before applying. The 16:45-17:15 UTC material sequence showed the 1730-1734 zone genuinely defended on real volume for 3 bars (including surviving an intrabar wick to 1730.18 at 17:00 UTC that a naive intrabar-stop system would have exited around breakeven-negative anyway) -- but the defense proved temporary; volume faded across that sequence (3562->3140->2281->1407) and the zone finally gave way on the 4th bar.

This is trade #48's genuine outcome, not forced into either a "stop management failed" or "stop management succeeded" narrative -- the close-based convention did exactly what it is designed to do (avoided a premature wick-based exit at 17:00 UTC that would have been worse or equal), and the eventual loss is simply the trade not working out, which is a normal and expected outcome for a disciplined system operating with defined risk.

POSITION: FLAT. Trade #48 CLOSED.

### TRADE #50 -- CLOSED (stop-out, close-based fill; IMPORTANT correction to "guaranteed profit" framing; trade-critical immediate write)
TIME: 2020-05-15 18:00:00 UTC (T=1589565600)
BAR: O 1748.232 / H 1748.895 / L 1741.283 / C 1742.366, volume 3422

Context: 17:30 UTC recovered strongly (vol1012, close 1749.361). 17:45 UTC made a fresh session high
(1751.718) but closed off it (vol1767, close 1748.232). This bar: a large real-volume (3422) reversal
-- open 1748.232, but a sharp ~7pt intrabar swing down to a low of 1741.283, closing at 1742.366. This
CLOSE is not just below the live stop (close-below-1746.998), it is also BELOW the 1744.135 entry
price itself. Per the close-based convention, EXIT PRICE = this bar's own close = 1742.366.

RESULT: entry 1744.135, exit 1742.366 -> **-1.769pts, LOSS-WITH-PLAN (clean)**.

CRITICAL HONEST CORRECTION: the 16:30 UTC trail was described as "locking in guaranteed profit"
(~2.863pts minimum if triggered from 1746.998). That framing was WRONG, and this trade is the direct
proof -- the close-based fill convention means the exit price is the triggering bar's own CLOSE, not
the nominal stop level. A single large-real-volume adverse bar can gap/plunge straight through the
stop level and close even further down, including below the stop AND below the entry price
simultaneously, exactly as happened here (bar range 1748.895 down to 1741.283, a 7.6pt swing). "The
stop is above entry" does NOT mean "the worst-case exit is profitable" under this convention -- it
only means the worst-case exit is bounded IF the triggering bar's close lands near the stop level,
which is not guaranteed when volatility/volume is elevated. This is a genuinely important, previously
unstated risk in how stops have been described this entire apprenticeship, and it is being corrected
here explicitly rather than smoothed over. Going forward, "locks in profit" language for a trailed
stop should be understood as "locks in a stop level above entry," NOT as a guarantee of a profitable
exit -- the actual exit depends on the triggering bar's full range/volatility.

Regarding the n=4 countertrend hypothesis: trade #50 is now the FOURTH consecutive countertrend LONG
loss this window (#47 -4.232, #48 -1.416, #49 -5.439, #50 -1.769), despite being the strongest-
confirmed entry, the most favorable intrabar development (reached +6.691pts unrealized intrabar at
17:45's high 1751.718 vs entry 1744.135), and disciplined stop trailing throughout. This is now a
much stronger signal than n=3: ALL FOUR countertrend LONGs against this BEARISH H4 context have lost
this window, via four different mechanisms (fast rejection / slow give-back / progressive large-
volume rejection / sharp reversal-through-trailed-stop). 

POSITION: FLAT. Trade #50 CLOSED.

RUNNING TALLY (50 closed trades): 16 wins-with-plan / 1 loss-without-plan(mistake) / 1
loss-via-management-mistake(TRADER_MISTAKE_004) / 32 losses-with-plan(clean) [was 31, +1]. Net:

was +10.265pts, trade #45). Honest close-out narrative: this was the FIRST WITH-trend (SHORT,
BEARISH H4) real-volume entry attempted this window, entered on exceptional confirmation (4532,

across the trade's life, surviving multiple large-volume tests (7576, 6438, 9045 among the largest
of the apprenticeship) and one sustained 4-bar consolidation battle that resolved in the trade's
favor, before finally giving back from its peak (+25.257pts) and closing out on a genuine trend
resumption/reversal at 16:30 UTC.

Contrast with the immediately preceding four countertrend LONG losses (#47-#50, all against this
same BEARISH H4 context): this is now genuine n=1 evidence that a clean, well-confirmed WITH-trend
setup can produce a dramatically different outcome than a countertrend one, even when both are
managed with the same close-based-fill discipline and trailing methodology. NOT concluding a
formal WITH-trend-vs-countertrend edge from n=1 -- but this is a strong, concrete data point
supporting the open hypothesis flagged after trade #50, and the largest single piece of evidence
this apprenticeship has produced either way.

Real-volume (3469) adverse reversal bar -- both the high (1735.927) and the close (1735.654) crossed
above the live stop (close-above-1734.37). Per the permanent close-based stop-trigger/fill
convention, EXIT PRICE = this bar's own close = 1735.654.

RESULT: entry 1733.911, exit 1735.654 (SHORT: profit = entry - exit) -> **-1.743pts,
LOSS-WITH-PLAN (clean)**.

Honest close-out narrative: this trade was managed with a genuinely TIGHT trail (0.459pts risk)
applied at bar 2 (12:30 UTC) after only 2 bars of real-volume continuation -- tighter than any
trail applied in trade #51 at a comparable point. The trade's own real-volume sequence reversed
sharply on the very next bar (3469 volume, a decisive close back above the recent lower-high),
stopping the trade out for a small loss. This is a genuine, honest lesson on trail tightness: the
3-bar real-volume sequence that justified the tight trail was itself not yet a fully established
pattern (only 2 bars of continuation before the trail, vs. trade #51's more developed structure
before its comparably tight moves) -- worth flagging as an open question about how much real-volume
continuation should be required before trailing this tightly, without concluding a hard rule from
n=1.

### TRADE #53 -- CLOSED (stop-out, close-based fill; another honest demonstration of the plunge-through-stop nuance; trade-critical immediate write)
TIME: 2020-05-19 15:00:00 UTC (T=1589900400)
BAR: O 1743.888 / H 1743.888 / L 1737.44 / C 1739.222, volume 2872

A sharp real-volume (2872) reversal bar -- close (1739.222) plunged well below the live stop
(close-below... wait, this is a LONG, stop triggers on close BELOW 1741.878) -- close 1739.222 is
2.656pts below the stop level itself, and also below the 1739.969 entry. Per the permanent
close-based stop-trigger/fill convention, EXIT PRICE = this bar's own close = 1739.222.

RESULT: entry 1739.969, exit 1739.222 (LONG: profit = exit - entry) -> **-0.747pts,
LOSS-WITH-PLAN (clean)**.

Honest close-out narrative, and an important repeat lesson: the 2nd trail (14:45 UTC) was described
as "locking in guaranteed profit" (~1.909pts minimum, stop at 1741.878 vs. entry 1739.969). That
framing was correct about the STOP LEVEL's relationship to entry, but this trade's own exit again
proves the standing corrected understanding (first learned in trade #50): a single large-volume
adverse bar can plunge straight through the stop level and close below both the stop AND the entry,
turning a nominal "guaranteed profit" trail into an actual loss. This is now the SECOND time this
exact mechanic has produced a losing exit from a trail that was described as profit-locking (trade
#50 being the first) -- worth treating as a now well-established pattern, not a one-off: trail
descriptions should always be read as "stop level vs. entry," never as a promise about the realized
exit, regardless of how many pips of buffer the stop appears to have.

Regarding the countertrend hypothesis: trade #53 was the strongest-confirmed countertrend LONG
attempt of the entire window, survived the two largest-volume adverse bars of the apprenticeship,
turned solidly profitable, and STILL closed as a loss (small, but a loss) when a final sharp
reversal plunged through its trail. This is now n=5 for countertrend LONGs against BEARISH H4 this
window: #47 -4.232, #48 -1.416, #49 -5.439, #50 -1.769, #53 -0.747 -- ALL FIVE have lost, though
this is easily the smallest-magnitude loss and the trade DID reach meaningful profit before giving
it back. The countertrend disadvantage hypothesis is now considerably stronger evidence (5/5
losses) even as the individual outcomes have gotten progressively closer to breakeven with stronger
confirmation and better management -- genuinely useful, nuanced evidence rather than a simple binary
verdict.

POSITION: FLAT. Trade #53 CLOSED.

in the trade's favor -- a wick-based stop system would have stopped this trade out here; the

### TRADE #54 -- CLOSED (stop-out, close-based fill; razor-thin trigger after surviving a much larger wick-through earlier; trade-critical immediate write)
TIME: 2020-05-20 18:00:00 UTC (T=1589997600)
BAR: O 1750.346 / H 1754.049 / L 1749.084 / C 1752.328, volume 1169

Cross-checked via count=3 re-fetch (critical bar, potential stop-out): confirmed finalized, exact
match to the live read.

This bar's CLOSE (1752.328) is 0.049pts above the stop level (close-based close ABOVE 1752.279) --
a razor-thin margin, on thin volume (1169), well below the real-volume threshold. Per the permanent
close-based stop-trigger/fill convention, the stop triggers purely on the close crossing the level,
regardless of volume. EXIT PRICE = this bar's own close = 1752.328.

RESULT: entry 1744.494, exit 1752.328 (SHORT: profit = entry - exit) -> **-7.834pts,
LOSS-WITH-PLAN (clean)**.

Notable honest contrast: this same trade survived a much LARGER wick-through at 13:45 UTC (high
1752.62, 0.341pts through the stop) without triggering, because that bar's close (1749.891) stayed
well below the level. Here, a comparatively unremarkable thin-volume bar closed just 0.049pts past
the same level and triggered the stop. This is a clean illustration of the close-based convention's
actual mechanics: proximity/wick depth is irrelevant, only the closing print matters, and a stop can
be taken out by a whisker-thin close on low volume just as easily as survive a much deeper wick on
high volume. No "mistake" here -- the convention was applied exactly as designed.

Regarding the WITH-trend hypothesis: this was the cleanest, most decisive WITH-trend entry of the
apprenticeship (2 consecutive real-volume closes lower, 2371/5219, the 2nd being the largest
directional move since trade #53's stress bars) -- stronger confirmation than trade #52's entry.
Despite that, and despite surviving a genuine stress test (2 consecutive massive-volume adverse bars,
one with a deep wick through the stop), the trade still lost, and lost MORE than trade #52 did
(-7.834 vs -1.743). WITH-trend n=3 this window: #51 WIN +22.386, #52 LOSS -1.743, #54 LOSS -7.834 --
2 losses out of 3, with the losses now outweighing the one win in aggregate (-9.577 vs +22.386, still
net positive but the win-rate itself is now 1/3). This meaningfully tempers the earlier tentative
lean toward "WITH-trend is safer than countertrend" -- entry-side confirmation strength did not
translate into a safer outcome here, and management (survived every test, never trailed since never
profitable) was arguably flawless. Worth treating as genuine, sobering evidence rather than dismissing
as one bad trade: quality of trigger and quality of management do not guarantee outcome even
WITH-trend.

POSITION: FLAT. Trade #54 CLOSED.

RUNNING TALLY (54 closed trades): 17 wins-with-plan / 1 loss-without-plan(mistake) / 1
loss-via-management-mistake(TRADER_MISTAKE_004) / 35 losses-with-plan(clean) [was 34, +1]. Net:
+18.908pts on closed trades (was +26.742, -7.834 this trade).

TIME: 2020-05-21 16:30:00 UTC (T=1590078600)
BAR: O 1724.152 / H 1726.872 / L 1723.856 / C 1725.33, volume 1379

Cross-checked via count=3 re-fetch (critical bar, potential stop-out): confirmed finalized, exact
match to the live read.

This bar's CLOSE (1725.33) is 0.05pts above the stop level (close-based close ABOVE 1725.28) -- an
even thinner margin than trade #54's own razor-thin trigger (0.049pts), on similarly unremarkable
volume (1379). Per the permanent close-based stop-trigger/fill convention, the stop triggers. EXIT
PRICE = this bar's own close = 1725.33.

RESULT: entry 1728.586, exit 1725.33 (SHORT: profit = entry - exit) -> **+3.256pts,
WIN-WITH-PLAN**.

This is a striking, deliberate contrast to trade #54's closure: both trades were stopped out by a
razor-thin close-only breach (0.05pts / 0.049pts) on unremarkable volume, with wick depth and volume
irrelevant either way -- but trade #54's trail was still above entry (a wide structural stop, never
trailed into profit territory) so its razor-thin trigger produced a loss, while trade #55's trail had
already been moved into profit territory (1725.28 vs entry 1728.586) after the position proved itself
with genuine structure, so its razor-thin trigger produced a win. This is the clearest illustration
yet that management quality (whether and when a stop gets moved into profit) determines whether a
razor-thin close-based trigger is good news or bad news -- the trigger mechanic itself is identical
either way.

Regarding the WITH-trend hypothesis: WITH-trend n=4 this window: #51 WIN +22.386, #52 LOSS -1.743,
#54 LOSS -7.834, #55 WIN +3.256. Now 2 wins / 2 losses -- a genuinely even record, further tempering
any presumption of directional safety. Aggregate WITH-trend P&L: +22.386-1.743-7.834+3.256 =

one) rather than a high win rate. Trade #55 also reinforces the trail-timing lesson from a positive
angle: the deliberate decision to NOT trail prematurely at 14:30 UTC (which would have mirrored trade

This trade's full arc is worth summarizing honestly: entered on one of the most decisive WITH-trend
confirmations of the apprenticeship (real-volume 5051/9575), reached as much as ~+9.039pts unrealized,
was trailed 5 times on genuinely confirmed multi-bar structure at each step (never prematurely, never
razor-thin at the moment of tightening), then had its final stop level (1712.888) tested closely by
wicks on roughly 6-7 separate bars across nearly 6 hours (13:45-00:30 UTC region, specifically the
19:45-23:45 UTC stretch) without ever triggering on a close -- until it finally did, at a solid
+5.857pts rather than scraping breakeven. This is a genuinely instructive counterpoint to trades #54
and #55's razor-thin outcomes: here, disciplined, patient trailing meant that even the "worst case"
resolution (eventual stop-out) still landed as a clear win, because each trail had been set with
enough structural distance rather than chasing the tightest possible level. The repeated close calls
at the same level did not indicate a flaw in the convention -- they simply reflected genuine price
consolidation right around a well-chosen structural level, and the close-based mechanic worked exactly
as designed throughout (multiple deeper wick-throughs survived, then a modest 0.1pts close-only breach
finally triggered).

Regarding the WITH-trend hypothesis: WITH-trend n=5 this window: #51 WIN +22.386, #52 LOSS -1.743, #54
LOSS -7.834, #55 WIN +3.256, #56 WIN +5.857 -- now 3 wins / 2 losses, aggregate +21.922pts. The win
rate has now tilted positive (3/5) for the first time in this window's WITH-trend sample, though still
too small to treat as validated. Trade #56 in particular reinforces the emerging practical lesson from
this cluster: trail timing and structural distance at each trail point appear to matter more for
outcome quality than raw entry-trigger strength, consistent with the trade #54/#55 comparison from

### ADMINISTRATIVE -- CEO CORRECTION: close-based trail is not a guaranteed-profit mechanism, reporting language corrected (immediate write, not smoothed over)
TIME OF CORRECTION: 2020-06-02, replay clock unchanged, trade #58 still open at the moment of
this correction (no bars skipped, no management action taken as a result of this entry itself).

ISSUE IDENTIFIED (by the CEO): two prior management entries for trade #58 this session used
"locks in a minimum of X points/R if subsequently stopped out" language for the first and second
trails. That phrasing is NOT mechanically valid under this apprenticeship's own permanent
close-based stop-trigger/fill convention: the stop level only defines the CLOSE-based trigger
threshold, not the fill price. The fill is always the triggering bar's own CLOSE, which can close
materially beyond the nominal stop level (in either direction) -- so no stop level, trailed or
otherwise, guarantees a minimum realized result. This has actually already been demonstrated
directly by this apprenticeship's own history: trade #54 stopped out at a close 0.049pts beyond
its nominal level, and multiple other trades have shown fills landing away from the exact nominal
stop price purely because that is how the close-based fill works.

AFFECTED ENTRIES (both already written this session, for trade #58):
- "FIRST TRAIL: stop moved from 1745.304 -> 1734.564 ... Locks in a minimum of +5.763pts (~1.16R)
  if subsequently stopped out." (TIME: 15:45 UTC)
- "SECOND TRAIL: stop moved from 1734.564 -> 1727.902 ... Locks in a minimum of +12.425pts
  (~2.50R) if subsequently stopped out." (TIME: 16:45 UTC)

CORRECTION (language/measurement only -- NOT a change to any frozen stop level, management
decision, or trade history): these two figures (+5.763pts/~1.16R and +12.425pts/~2.50R) are
correctly computed as the TRAIL_TRIGGER_LEVEL_R -- the result IF a future bar's close landed
exactly at the nominal stop price -- but were incorrectly described as guaranteed/locked-in
minimums. They are not. The ACTUAL REALIZED_RESULT_R for trade #58, whenever it closes, will be
computed from the true triggering bar's own close (or from ongoing favorable price action if the
trade is later closed by further trailing/reaching a natural conclusion), exactly as this
apprenticeship's TRADE_EVIDENCE_LOG.md has always done for every prior closed trade (e.g. trade
#57's exit was fixed at 1712.302, the triggering bar's actual close, not its nominal stop of
1710.66).

TERMINOLOGY ADOPTED GOING FORWARD (measurement discipline only, no trading-rule change):
- TRAIL_TRIGGER_LEVEL_R: the R-multiple corresponding to the nominal stop price at the moment of
  any trail -- a reference figure only, computed as (entry - nominal_stop) / INITIAL_RISK_POINTS
  for a SHORT.
- REALIZED_RESULT_R: the actual R-multiple from the true fill price at close, computed only once
  a trade genuinely closes. Never assumed, never described as "guaranteed" while a trade remains
  open.
While a trade is open, any reference to a trail level's approximate R will use language of the
form "current trail trigger corresponds to approximately +X R at the stop level, but realized R is
not guaranteed because fill occurs at the triggering bar's own close" -- not "locks in" or
"guaranteed minimum."

VERIFICATION OF EXISTING ACCOUNTING: STATIC_BASELINE and ACTUAL_MANAGEMENT figures already logged
in TRADE_EVIDENCE_LOG.md for every closed trade (through #57) were checked and confirmed to already
use actual close-based fill prices throughout, never nominal stop prices -- e.g. trade #57's
STATIC_RESULT_POINTS/ACTUAL_RESULT_POINTS both used the true fill (1712.302), consistent with the
methodology doc's own definition. No retroactive correction to any closed trade's figures is
needed; only the "locks in minimum" narrative phrasing on trade #58's still-open management
entries was incorrect, and is corrected here going forward.

CLOSE_BASED_TRAIL_ACCOUNTING = PASS (existing R/points accounting for closed trades was already
correct; only forward narrative language for the still-open trade #58 needed correction)
TRADE_58_MANAGEMENT_CHANGED = NO
TRADE_58_FROZEN_LEVELS_CHANGED = NO
